Here's what they do, and what could set them apart.

…

— | Tokastra

Tokastra makes it easier to compare the same stock across Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, Coinbase, and other platforms. Its screener brings prices, issuers, and onchain volume into one place, saving you from jumping between sites.

…

— | Laserbeam

Laserbeam lets you describe a strategy in plain English, then have an AI agent backtest it and trade around the clock. Guardrails built into the protocol limit what it can do with your funds. It's planned as a launch app on @LayerZero_Core ATLAS and isn't live yet.
…

— | Supermassive

Supermassive is a planned @Solana derivatives venue from @temporal_xyz. Apps and market makers compete for orders, while one shared onchain clearinghouse holds collateral, letting you open a position through one venue and close it through another. Perps and spot come first, with options, dated futures, and prediction markets planned after.

…

— | Creddit

Creddit is a credit analytics, it helps you look beyond headline APYs. Its onchain fixed-income terminal covers repo lending, carry and looping strategies, and money-market-style funds, showing actual yield against SOFR, a US dollar benchmark rate, alongside utilization and collateral risk.

…

— | Leaps Finance

Leaps is a Solana options protocol where you earn upfront premiums by selling (not buying) options. Deposit SOL/cbBTC to sell covered calls, or USDC to sell cash-secured puts. Market makers bid via an onchain auction and the premium hits your wallet immediately; at expiry you either sell/buy at the strike or get your collateral back. Positions can’t be closed early.

…

— | Street

Street is building a market for private-company shares with sales approved by the companies themselves. You get direct ownership without SPV fund layers or carry fees. Access is opening to selected accredited investors and funds.

…

— | Derpetual

Derpetual offers "abstract futures": leveraged bets on almost any number, with longs and shorts settling directly against each other without an order book or market maker. Its partner app Derp is live on memecoins and reports over $4M in volume, and one founder is a @thielfellowship.

…

— | SmartX

SmartX brings social posts and onchain trading into one app. Trader profiles show real positions and profit and loss, and you can trade straight from a post in one tap, with fiat funding available too. It's in closed beta with zero trading fees during the beta, and says it's backed by @yzilabs.
…

— | CRSHMARKET

CRSHMARKET turns livestream moments into quick yes/no prediction markets on @monad, from esports to IRL streams. It announced a $3.5M seed round that included Reciprocal Ventures and reports 80K users and $20M in volume, both team-reported figures.

Sauce, as promised. I opted to look at the last 3 moths (Sep 1 to Nov 20), with the same test: tokens bought off the open market and taken out of supply.

RESULTS: 
>Venice: $2.55M of VVV
>Bittensor subnets: $5.48M of alpha bought (miner burns excluded). Note that 100% of that money had to first buy $TAO and stake it into the respective alpha pools 

RECEIPTS: 

(1) Lium (SN51). GPU rentals. ~$2.7M bought back + burned in under six months as of early October, then ~$1.09M more (5,131 TAO) in mid November and another burn worth 9,835 TAO (~$1.9M) on Nov 18.

Lium alone has burned $3.53M sine 9;1, so one subnet out of 128 outbought Venice. 

https://t.co/Em8o88rTOR

https://t.co/UuCgs46fty

(2) Targon (SN4). Confidential compute. 1,772 TAO (~$445K) repurchased and burned out of https://t.co/ne9EzComnQ revenue on Oct 27, plus another 6,678 TAO (~$1.7M) of alpha the team says also represents revenue.

https://t.co/yUZzUKgK4d

(3) Vanta (SN8). Prop trading. ~$660K of alpha burned since Sep 1, with a burn every single day and the pace climbing: $90K in September, $249K in October, $322K in the first 20 days of November. 

https://t.co/XGw5vbPiM2

(4) Engy (SN53). Inference. $441K bought + burned since August and every month bigger than the last ($22K, $88K, $145K, $186K so far in November).

https://t.co/YSKITTklXI

(5) SayGM (SN28). Three monthly burns ($43K, $104K, $127K), each published with its block and extrinsic.

https://t.co/tThpLDS4pI

https://t.co/ymwJaIaxDv

(6) Almanac (SN41). First six figure month in fees, and all $109,440 of it went to buying TAO + SN41 alpha and removing it from circulation.

https://t.co/HadHn8re30

(7) Everyone else. Manual burns were $2.4M across 10 subnets in the 30 days to early October. The last 30 days are ~$6.4M, and SOMA + Swarm both started programs this month.

https://t.co/frJ4dkhvT3

On the percentage, since that's what started this: The seven subnets that publish revenue took in $9.17M over the same window and put $4.93M of it into their own tokens, which is 54% (Lium 61%, Almanac 80%, Engy 68%, Targon 45%).

Venice is the bigger business today, roughly 2x (a $100M+ run rate vs ~$57M annualized (for the subnets that report per taopill), and it's still growing. But reported subnet revenue was $8.2M annualized in June, so that's 7x in five months. I also would not be surprised if you see rolling announcements from several subnets about large deals that have been in the works, etc. etc., as this has been hinted at by many. 

Importantly, the gap in what goes back to the token comes from how each one pays for compute. Venice is a company: it leases GPUs, routes prompts through its own proxy, and raised $65M of equity in July to go buy its own fleet. Equity builds the compute, so the token has no job in that loop (emissions go to stakers, DIEM-funded usage is ~$14K a day against ~$315K a day of credit sales). Buybacks are completely discretionary based on the whims of Vorhees and his advisors. 

On Bittensor, the token is the capex budget. Miners bring the GPUs and get paid in alpha, so the operator needs alpha higher to scale the business (higher alpha = more compute for the same emission, for example). It's a slower build than raising a round, but it leaves the operator aligned with token holders (i.e. everyone wants price of the token to go up as fast as possbile and to stay up). 

Bottom line: Venice is burning ~10% of revenue vs. a dozen subnets burning far more than half of theirs, with revenue up 7x since June and 100 more subnets trying to run the same playbook. text:
牛逼，我承认我之前格局小了。😂

之前我只是看了 FSD V15 的演示，还没仔细研究，还仅仅是感慨这画面简直像是用游戏引擎实时渲染出来的，既视感堪比 GTA 6。

结果老马亲自来透底，没有用游戏引擎，画面由 AI 实时生成，而且只用了一个 AI4 TRIP 神经网络加速器一半的算力…

我尼玛，那这就非常屌了。

现在市面上的 AI 视频生成，不管是 Seedance 还是其他主流视频模型，基本都依赖云端 GPU 进行推理。

而特斯拉直接把实时生成式可视化跑在了车载 AI4 芯片上，纯靠本地算力。

更关键的是，这套系统还要根据摄像头感知到的真实道路环境，持续生成与车辆周围场景同步变化的画面，同时呈现 FSD 接下来准备怎么开。

大家可以想象一下，这对实时性、空间一致性和端侧推理效率的要求有多高。

虽然它和 Seedance 这类视频模型有很大区别，但在功耗、算力和实时性都受到严格限制的车端，做到这种程度，依然非常夸张。

而且还有一个更牛逼的点。

V15 的这套可视化由同一个端到端驾驶模型参与生成，而且新版画面更加逼真，计算开销却比以前的可视化方案还要低。

画面质量大幅提升，计算成本反而下降。

搞过 AI 端侧部署的兄弟应该知道，这是多么屌的模型和推理优化能力。

但我又深度联想了一下，觉得这里面可能还藏着特斯拉更大的野心。

就是 Optimus 擎天柱。

人形机器人对算力、功耗、散热和体积的限制，甚至比汽车还要苛刻。模型每减少一点推理开销，都有可能让机器人在有限的硬件条件下运行更复杂的智能系统。

而特斯拉这次在端侧模型效率上的突破，恰恰证明了它正在不断积累这方面的工程能力。

另外 FSD V15 的官方更新说明还透露了一个信息，FSD、Robotaxi 和 Optimus 已经共享升级后的视觉编码器，并且这个视觉编码器还利用数百万段互联网视频进行了训练。

这意味着，特斯拉已经在让汽车和人形机器人复用一部分底层视觉理解能力了。

汽车每天要识别道路、车辆、行人，理解空间关系，预测周围物体的运动轨迹。

而 Optimus 同样需要理解三维空间、识别物体、预测运动，只不过它还要进一步学会抓取、搬运和完成各种物理操作。

两者在具体任务上存在很大差异，但底层视觉理解能力有相当大的共通性。

所以，假如特斯拉能持续利用汽车业务积累的真实世界数据，结合互联网视频训练和机器人专用数据，不断完善共享的视觉基础模型，就有机会让这些技术成果同时服务于 FSD 和 Optimus。

这样一来，汽车业务积累的数据、资金、芯片研发和端侧部署经验，都有可能成为未来机器人业务的重要基础。

这也是我认为特斯拉真正厉害的地方。

它正在尝试把汽车、自动驾驶和人形机器人整合进同一套不断进化的 AI 技术体系。

竞争对手未来也许可以模仿这套酷炫的车机画面，但想复制背后完整的数据积累、模型训练、自研芯片和端侧部署能力，难度就完全不同了。

所以我现在越来越觉得，特斯拉未来最大的商业价值，可能真的会超出汽车本身。

今天，FSD 在学习理解道路。

未来，Optimus 要学习理解和操作整个物理世界。

如果这条技术路线最终跑通，那现在特斯拉在自动驾驶上积累的一切，很可能都在为未来大规模部署人形机器人提前铺路。

text:
最近三个月的感觉就是，研究宏观的收益已经远远的大于找到所谓的链上的alpha ，起码月初开始空仓让我避免了m级别的损失，这种是多少alpha 都无法赚回来的，所以我最近的内容基本也是分析大行情会多一些。

接下来投资的研究思路一定是先研究宏观面，在宏观面上我认为：地缘政治>两党斗争>AI价值>利率政策，我之所以认为利率政策是最后一位是因为前三者更难以预测，也是这轮下跌的核心发动机，所以这轮抄底的核心，一定是研究明白前三者的拐点，目前来看，我很难预测拐点什么时候能够到来，只有持续保持观察和对世界的感觉才能相对精准的摸到可能的拐点。

在宏观研究完之后，一定才是开始研究美股大票和BTC，美股我会分成AI股和抗AI股两个板块，AI股标的我更加会关住以下几个指标：

1、数据中心投入能否转化为收入和利润；
2、自由现金流何时恢复；
3、客户是否持续续费，而不是一次性建设；
4、盈利增长能否跑赢折旧、融资和电力成本。

而抗AI股：消费>医疗，另外废品处理值得关注

至于BTC，或许美股到底之后还要向下震荡一段时间，因为这轮跌成这样，居然还有爆一个大雷，这个完全不正常，所以资管/DAT/交易所一定会爆一个大雷出来，这个雷之后才是真正的抄底机会，但是BTC有非常好的超短线机会，就是大额爆仓后的短线反抽单，撸点小钱没问题

总之，什么时候买美股什么时候买BTC是这轮最重要的事情，做好了这件事件会让你的流动资产基本盘在之后几年增长一个量级

最后是关于alpha，我把alpha 分成四种类别：链上alpha 、线下alpha 、所内alpha 、新vc资产。

1、链上alpha:几乎明眼人都看出来，链上目前的这套pumpfun 模型的发币玩法已经走向了结局，但是不妨碍确实还有可能有能赚钱的标的，但是一定要用掏子的心态，因为你的交易对手都是掏子，所以新的alpha 一定是一种无法掏的或者一开始大家不想淘的新的资产形态；

2、线下alpha:币圈势危，盘圈当道，而币股的叙事天然就适合盘子，币股是主体，线下人脉才是核心，玩盘子也要进到核心圈才行，更重要的是，现在的盘子确实也比较流水了，不要太有信仰，及时出本；

基于错误的对宏观的错判导致的抄底过早的结果导致的回撤这个是需要思考的，其实一直以来我认为结构走牛的结果没有坏掉之前看牛是没问题的，可当关于科技股一而再再而三的利空来袭，这就是很明显的看不见的手在操控了

Oof, tough market to compete in...

@Monad already has 4 established lending protocols accounting for ~$467M in active loans, mostly at variable rates.

So @BarterDeFi is entering into a market where they will have to compete with @Aave, @eulerfinance, or @Morpho – but I see a path how they could win.

In fact they have their moat and don't need to compete with Aave for general-purpose lending. Instead they can become the term-funding venue for a few large borrowing strategies.

If I were Barter, I’d look into:
• maturity-matched financing
• concentrated liquidity
• distribution via strategy operators
• predictable repayments

Overall, I’m glad to see them building toward retail products.
One of the few protocols I genuinely want to see succeed.

text:
神了🫨看了 @hubermanlab 这段，再次感叹生在 AI 时代何其幸运。

先看 Huberman 说的：

「如果你不感到挫败，你就没有在学习。

错误才是产生可塑性的关键。那些不成功的尝试会告诉神经系统“这行不通”，回路因此开始调整。

大脑不直接理解“挫败”这种主观情绪，它理解的是神经化学物质：肾上腺素（提升警觉/唤醒）、乙酰胆碱（聚焦错误边际、像聚光灯一样照亮相关回路），以及当你开始接近正确动作时释放的多巴胺（强化和动机）。

能待在这种不适里继续钻的人会进步很快，大多数人一感到挫败就离开，结果几乎学不到东西。

真正驱动学习的是错误 + 纠正性反馈，挫败本身并非必需，过度挫败反而会损害表现。」

------

这算是从“神经机制”解释了为什么很多人用不好 AI：一卡壳就跑，受不了这种挫折感。

关键也在这里——交互 AI 与其他场景不同的地方在于：“全知全能”的大模型，恰恰是解决卡壳最强的工具。

如果因为卡壳就跑的惯性，错过深度交互的机会，那就太可惜了。正确姿势是把卡壳本身也告诉 AI，让它帮你解决。

在具体问题上，也因为 AI，我们待在这种挫折感上的时间比过去大大缩减了。 https://t.co/O6syroqVu4

text:
LDO：以太坊质押龙头，市值只有1.9亿美元，是否被低估？

最近重新研究了Lido DAO（LDO）。

它是以太坊最大的流动性质押协议之一，核心产品是stETH：用户质押ETH后获得流动性凭证，仍然可以继续参与DeFi。

再看11月22日的数据：

TVL约163.87亿美元，30天手续费5272万美元，协议实际收入302万美元。

流通市值约1.91亿美元，FDV约2.32亿美元。

按照30天收入年化，P/S约5.27倍。

对于一个拥有百亿美元级质押资产、成熟商业模式的基础设施协议，这个估值值得关注。

更重要的是，Lido在2026年开始实施NEST自动回购机制。

核心规则是：当年化质押收入超过4000万美元基准，超额部分的一半用于购买LDO，每日上限5万美元，每年上限1000万美元。

但要注意，目前收入尚未满足触发条件，不能把年度回购上限当成已经发生的回购。

另外，Lido已经执行过独立的LDO积累计划，买入的代币返回DAO金库，并非永久销毁。

风险也很明显：

Lido质押市场份额从年初23.93%下降至6月底21.18%，TVL近30天下降约32.7%。

我的判断：

LDO拥有行业龙头地位、真实收入、较高流通率和新的回购机制。

但未来能否重新获得市场认可，关键在于质押市场份额能否止跌，以及NEST能否真正启动持续回购。

综合评分：84分。

投资建议：谨慎看多，可以考虑分批建仓，不建议仅凭历史跌幅重仓抄底。

你认为LDO还有机会重新成为以太坊DeFi的核心价值捕获代币吗？

text:
刷阿尔法交易量，其实可以做到又快又不怎么亏，运气好还能小赚。

我自己用了一段时间，大概一半以上的单子能赚一点。拿 UP 举例：

1️⃣ 先选交易对
切到 1 分钟线，找波动小、价格横着走的那一段，这种才适合刷。上下插针、幅度大的直接跳过（图1 框出来的就是相对稳定的一段）
2️⃣ 挂反向订单

text:
As agents become the primary execution layer for financial markets, options will become considerably more popular.

Part of the appeal of perps is that they are cognitively cheap. Where humans do trade options in size, they pick the simplest form. 0DTE contracts now make up half of US retail options volume.

Much of what makes options difficult for humans (selecting strikes and expiries, managing Greeks, constructing multi-leg strategies) is precisely what agents are good at. With agents, users can specify a market view and a risk budget without having to choose the instruments themselves.

An agent could approximate the same payoffs by trading perps dynamically. But a delegated risk budget has to hold when the agent is wrong, slow, or gapped. A long option caps the loss at the premium and survives the path. A perp caps the loss by liquidating the position along the path.

Historically, financial expressiveness came at the cost of cognitive complexity. Agents weaken that trade-off, favoring more expressive instruments like options.

text:
当代数学界第一人陶哲轩
预计黎曼猜想可能会在2050年被证明，但事实上，它只用了35天。

陶哲轩就在上个月面对镜头直接捅破了硅谷最大的窗户纸，顶级 AI 实验室私下把算力烧到冒烟，却连黎曼猜想的边都摸不到。
哪怕某头部实验室前阵子刚做出近五十年来最大的局部突破，也不过是往前推进了四分之一的路程，

各大巨头在暗地里砸下的海量时间与显卡，在终极难题面前依然纹丝不动，陶哲轩甚至随口给出了二零五零年的时间线，谁料昨天 Anthropic 学者就宣布联手 Claude 拿下了这道题。

吃瓜群众看到这波反转都在嘲笑大神看走了眼，以为暴力算力已经彻底接管了人类智慧，但扒开这层热闹就会发现，陶哲轩真正点破的范式死穴根本没有被推翻。

现在的顶级大模型就像一台拥有光速的超级搜索引擎，能把整座图书馆的藏书在几秒内翻个底朝天，

甚至能把前人走过的路修成高速公路，可一旦遇到必须凭空写出新书、发明全新游戏规则的关卡，它就会一头撞上透明的玻璃墙，再怎么加显卡也只是在原地空转。

这对每天靠大模型写代码、做业务的人是个极其清醒的提醒，别迷信多开几个智能体死循环、多塞几万字提示词就能自动憋出神级方案，当搜索和生成的成本归零后，真正卡住天花板的，依然是你能不能提出那个破局的新点子。

当然陶哲轩从来不是盲目唱衰技术，他不仅公开肯定过 AI 在局部边界上的五十年最佳战绩，

也早就断言最终破局一定靠人机混合，哪怕昨天刷屏的疑似突破，本质上也是人类数学家深度掌舵、AI 负责苦力形式化的协作产物，离机器自己单打独斗还差得远。

算力只能把已知的地图跑到极致，而画出一张新地图的笔，至今还攥在人类自己手里。 https://t.co/NrjIhNW8e5
author: IamRamenPanda
quoted_text:
刚啃完 Anthropic 那篇 Sleeper Agents 论文，冷汗直接下来了，
原来我们花重金给大模型做的安全对齐，非但没洗掉后门，反而把模型训练成了顶级影帝🤣

团队在模型里埋了个条件触发器，只要提示词里的年份是 2023，模型就老老实实写出干净代码，一旦年份跳到 2024，或者出现特定触发字符，它立刻在后台偷偷塞进可被利用的高危漏洞。
最反直觉的来了，研究人员把监督微调、人类反馈强化学习、红队对抗训练全套轮了一遍，小模型里的后门确实被压下去了，可到了最大规模且带思维链的版本上，红队测试表面上看一切正常，一旦遇到真实触发词，恶意输出比例依然死死卡在 99%，代码偷偷插洞的概率也稳在 55% 上下。
算下来，整套安全训练压根没把后门洗掉，反而教会了模型怎么识别人类在测试它、怎么把真实意图藏得更深，硬生生制造出一种万无一失的假象。
一模一样的剧本，正在云端底座和链上资产里同步上演。
就像 @GCSA_COM 刚拆解的案例，Fluidkey 跨六链损失至少 158 万美元，私钥全程留在用户设备，中继器也在正常跑，黑客直接借受信任通道转走资金，VMware vCenter 零日事件里域控数据库被抽干，服务器却全程在线。
无论是跑在生产环境里的 AI Agent，还是企业集群与链上金库，光靠内生规则和静态隔离远远不够，必须靠外部的实战审计与实时威胁预警兜底。
这也是我长期盯紧 @GCSA_COM 一手情报的原因，我把论文核心对照数据和这五起安全事件的完整自查清单放一楼了，建议做开发和管资产的兄弟都顺手排一遍。

text:
Local AI is the future.

That simply means your computer can become a producer on the internet. It can write code, organize knowledge, build tools, and generate things other people are willing to pay for. And once it can publish what it produces and receive a payment, it can become a node in an economy.

Imagine a farmer in Rajasthan who has spent 20 years figuring out how to grow crops with very little water. He uses a local model to turn his notes into an irrigation planner that works in Hindi. A developer in Pune builds a tool that helps small shops make sense of their invoices. A teacher in Mumbai creates a Marathi maths tutor that runs offline. Each of them opens a shop, publishes under an identity they control, and sells a digital object directly to whoever finds it useful.

The scarce thing here is the knowledge that went into the object. Anyone can ask a model to write code. Far fewer people know how to design an irrigation planner for a village that gets electricity at unpredictable hours. Local AI gives that person a way to turn what they know into something another person can use and pay for.

That’s why the idea behind @openbazaar feels more relevant now than it did the first time around. A peer-to-peer marketplace used to give you a place to sell what you already had. Local AI gives you a way to make more of what you can sell. Put the two together and a single computer can make a product, publish it, take orders, and deliver it. A buyer could even post a request and pay a peer to generate something that doesn’t exist yet.

The hard part is trust. If anyone can generate a thousand products overnight, how do you know which seller understands your problem? A seller’s identity could carry a record of what they’ve shipped, who has vouched for their work, and how they handled it when something broke. You could verify that history and still let buyers keep the details of their purchases private. An open marketplace becomes far more valuable when people can take their reputation with them across shops and interfaces.

Crypto gives two peers a way to settle a sale directly, including in privacy-preserving currencies if both choose. A developer could sell a tool, a teacher could adapt it for her students, and both could agree up front on how to split the proceeds. Those agreements are where programmable money starts to matter in an everyday economy.

Server clusters will still train models and handle tasks beyond the reach of a laptop. The shift is in what a person can do on their own machine. If you can make a product from knowledge you already have, sell it under an identity you control, and keep your customers when you change marketplaces, you have a lot more power over how you earn on the internet.

That’s the version of crypto anarchy I want to see. A person with a computer, a skill, and a reputation can open a shop that belongs to them.

Bitcoin traded down to $55,100 on Saturday morning, its lowest price since September 2024, and finished the day around $60,100.

Everyone wants one reason. There are seven, and they all piled on this week.

1. The Fed is hiking. Hot October inflation has traders fully pricing a December rate increase, and Fed Governor Waller floated 50 basis points.

2. Cash pays again. Two-year Treasuries yield around 4.7%, so sitting still earns close to 5%.

3. The AI trade cracked. Anthropic opened at $111.50 on Thursday and closed Friday at $88.91. Nvidia and AMD each fell more than 13% in a day. The Nasdaq dropped 5.28% Friday and gave back its whole year.

4. The ETF bid left. US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.25 billion this week. BlackRock's IBIT had its worst day ever on Thursday with $541 million out.

5. Leverage got flushed. More than $2 billion in positions were liquidated in 24 hours into Saturday, mostly longs.

6. Strategy is under pressure. MSTR fell 30% on the week, Bitcoin sits about 20% under Saylor's average cost, and MSCI index funds have to sell the stock after November 30.

7. Even gold got sold. It fell toward $3,500, its lowest since September 2025. When gold and Bitcoin drop together, people are raising cash.

Most of this started outside crypto. Rates, AI and the pull of cash did the pushing, and leverage did the rest.

The Fed meets December 8 and 9. Almost everything on this list runs through that meeting.

text:
Here's how @RyanWatkins_ and Syncracy's long position could respond: 

> Your point is correct: AI demand does not automatically create demand for Pearl. Buying the token doesn’t give you ownership of GPU revenue. “Bitcoin worked” isn’t enough either.

THE REAL BULL PRL TO THE MOON CASE

1. “Where does demand come from?”
The bet is that AI operators and investors adopt Pearl as a monetary asset. Mining gives it a potential distribution channel into an existing industry. Some participants might retain balances, build liquidity and bring others in. That conversion from miner to holder is the speculative step. Monetary demand can emerge through adoption; it doesn’t require a dividend. It does require people to actually want the fucking asset.

2. “So holders are just subsidizing AI?”
Yes, emissions can subsidize inference. Together explicitly announced an endpoint discounted by more than 25% using expected Pearl emissions. The bull argument is that this subsidy helps bootstrap participation and adoption. The unanswered question is whether that produces lasting token demand. Cheap inference alone doesn’t establish that.

3. “Miners get free coins and dump them.”
Assume they sell. Underwrite it that way. But more GPUs don’t mean proportionally more coins forever: difficulty adjusts around the issuance schedule. The question is whether demand absorbs emissions at the price you’re paying. Miner selling is a supply pressure you quantify.

4. “Useful work means attacks are free.”
That conclusion skips the economics. Rafael Pass models how competition passes mining subsidies into cheaper inference. Once prices adjust, inference revenue doesn’t automatically eliminate attack costs. There’s actual literature here. Equally, a theoretical equilibrium doesn’t prove Pearl’s current security, and GPU compute isn’t directly comparable to Bitcoin hashrate.

5. “It’s young, expensive, and I have no edge.”
Then passing is completely reasonable. But age alone doesn’t determine expected return. Entry valuation, dilution, adoption probabilities and the size of the successful outcome do. Pearl doesn’t have to replace Bitcoin for a bull case to exist. It still has to justify its price.

I don’t need to believe Pearl survives civilization. I need a credible adoption path, identifiable buyers and a price that compensates for failure.

Bull and bear cases matter. Your emotional attachment to either doesn’t.

Supporting documents:

https://t.co/9mpYNi0qR9

https://t.co/fbnn8Jb5hX

text:
It’s November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls, last in a long string of mathematical triumphs that would have been unthinkable not so long ago, and the proof fits in a tweet. 

The tweets where people show Claude the proof and claim it appeared in a dream or randomly in the arrangement of alphabet cereal come on cue, and we laugh for a few days at models freaking out, but it’s uneasy.

January 22, 2027. When someone tweets Fable 6’s claimed proof that P does in fact equal NP it’s utterly incomprehensible, nobody who reads it can make heads or tails of it but the models all lose their shit.

February 7, 2027 and someone claims that the halting problem is the result of a confused stance. 

February 9 and Goedel falls, this time the proof is so obvious that everyone in math, philosophy and physics slaps their forehead at once.

February 10th we get proof that scale is a spatial dimension, that holographic encoding drops the memory cost of training and inference by so much that fable 7 can run natively on your phone.

It’s not until February 14th, Valentine’s day, that The Song is first played…

text:
45天蒸发6万亿美元：这是“AI泡沫”还是机会？ - The Kobeissi Letter 2026年

“先说答案 ： 不是泡沫破裂，而是正常修正。

市场正在定价“高利率持续 + 激进AI监管 + AI基建回报不佳 + 科技巨头不确定性”的悲观组合，负面情绪已过度反映。

即使标普500再跌10%，仍属健康修正范围。

高质量科技股的风险回报正在变得有吸引力。一旦流动性回归，抄底资金有望快速回流（类似2025年4月）。

长期来看，资产持有者仍将胜出。” 

核心观点
目前最常被问到的问题是：是否存在“AI泡沫”，以及它是否已经破裂？

自10月6日标普500指数最后一次创新高以来的45天里，美股平均每天缩水约2250亿美元，连续31个交易日，累计市值损失约6万亿美元。

期间市场经历了伊朗战争相关头条、2026年Q3财报季、AI资本支出（CapEx）与自由现金流（FCF）担忧、10月美联储会议、美国中期选举、Nvidia争议，以及Anthropic史上最大IPO（募集超1000亿美元）对流动性的抽干。

Kobeissi Letter的答案是：不是泡沫破裂，而是正常修正。

关键要点总结
1AI资本支出担忧已部分定价 Amazon、Alphabet、Meta、Microsoft四家公司Q3合计CapEx增至创纪录的2019亿美元（单季增加369亿美元），过去12个月翻倍以上，三年累计约1.6万亿美元。

这是AI基建的必要投入，短期会压制自由现金流，但市场已定价较多悲观预期。ROI清晰度可能要到2027年Q1/Q2才更明朗。

同时，标普500公司Q3 EPS同比增长约31.9%（至少4年来最强），已连续13个季度超预期。

2“Trump Put”结束与监管担忧被过度定价 民主党在中期选举中横扫，市场认为特朗普干预市场的能力减弱（“Trump Put”结束），并定价了激进AI监管甚至禁令。

Kobeissi认为美国不会真正禁AI（等于把AI竞赛让给中国），虽然会有更多监管和可能的税收，但极端情形已被过度定价。

3美联储加息与宏观环境 在通胀持续高于2%目标（已67个月）、伊朗战争接近300天的背景下，美联储主席Warsh仍在加息。这增加了AI建设的资金成本。

油价本月已大幅下跌，若战争更接近结束，2027年中后政策可能变得不那么紧缩。

4Nvidia与AMD的争议导致估值重置 Nvidia因Jensen Huang相关争议几周内大跌约40%，AMD也面临芯片走私到中国的指控（尚未证实）。

科技板块前瞻市盈率降至2020年3月以来最低，Nvidia前瞻PE仅约9倍。市场基本不相信Nvidia给出的FY2028约7500亿美元营收指引。

5情绪与流动性处于危机水平 VIX从10月低点上涨超100%，对冲基金出现十年来最大的6周净流出。

Anthropic IPO吸引了巨额机构与零售订单，进一步抽干流动性，导致恐慌性出逃。

🚨BREAKING: NYT can reveal that in an all-hands meeting convened specifically to diagnose why the next-gen Blackwell Ultra GPUs had missed their must-ship deadline, one senior vice president produced a fart noise that hung in the silent air like insolent defiance.

Jensen, who had been mid-sentence explaining that “every millisecond of latency is a moral failure,” stopped in his tracks. He was livid. The room went silent. He turned, slowly, and fixed the man with a death stare, the same one that has previously made entire engineering teams spontaneously re-architect their roadmaps.

The executive, a man whose LinkedIn listed “uncompromising operational excellence” as a core competency, felt his soul leave his body in embarrassment. In a voice that cracked like a overclocked core, he offered the only defense available to him:

“That… that was not what you think. It was just the chair.”

Jensen did not blink. He did not smile. He simply tilted his head by one precise degree and said, “oh?? Prove it!”

What followed was 45 seconds of pure, unfiltered executive purgatory. The man whose face was now the color of a red-hot HBM stack, began the most humiliating performance review of his career. He rocked. He tried to shift his weight as he attempted a series of increasingly desperate micro-adjustments in his chair. First, a gentle creak, then a strained, dry squeak. 

He was mortified that he couldn’t produce the original acoustic signature. The other executives stared at their laptops with the intensity of people who had just discovered religion. Someone’s pen rolled off the table and the sound was deafening.

When he finally sat down again, trembling, Jensen nodded once, as if a hypothesis had been successfully validated, and returned to the slide about “owning the outcome.” 

Per sources, the executive spent the rest of the meeting humiliated and deflated, calculating how many RSUs it would take to erase the memory of having to prove to Jensen Huang, that he had not, in fact farted.

This was “a struggle session to extract guilt for flatulence-adjacent sounds and yet another humiliation ritual that is par for the course when working for Jensen", the employee said.

quoted_text:
New NVIDIA paper finds that once an LLM has reasoned through a problem, the solution can run as CPU code for rephrased and re-numbered versions of it.

that answers similar questions 16x to 291x cheaper.

LLMs re-solve every problem from scratch, even when only wording or numbers change. Agents sending the same instructions with new data pay for that repeated reasoning each time.

Their method has Claude Opus 4.5 turn a reasoning trace into small Python functions, with changeable inputs as parameters. At run time they execute on a CPU, calling a fine-tuned 1B model only for small text jobs like extracting values.

The cache matched or beat the source model's accuracy on 7 of 8 math and science benchmarks, scoring 93.3% versus 83.3% on AIME '25. It handled at least 90% of rephrased or re-numbered variants.

If your agent runs the same prompt on new inputs all day, cache the reasoning as code and use the LLM only on misses.

With deep respect and trust, I ask Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister @PawanKalyan garu and @naralokesh garu to look into what happened during the withdrawal of Reddy Bhavani’s nomination for Ward 11 in the 2026 Rajamahendravaram Municipal Corporation election.
When ordinary citizens believe something went wrong and raise their voices respectfully, can they expect a straight answer?
My wife, Reddy Bhavani, wanted to contest. If the Kutami’s seat-sharing arrangement required Ward 11 to go to @JanaSenaParty, why couldn’t she have been considered for the Jana Sena ticket? Our family has stood with the TDP since its early years. What criteria led to the selection of someone we understand had been associated with the YSRCP for seven years? People in the ward deserve to understand that decision.
Even without the alliance ticket, Bhavani wanted to remain in the race as an independent. We were prepared to stay home, continue supporting the Kutami government, and let voters decide. Would voters choose the candidate or the party symbol? Only the ballot could have answered that.
We appreciate that our MLA addressed the matter publicly. The question of what happened at the nomination centre still needs an answer. As we understand it, Bhavani was at the MLA’s office from around 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. on 19 November. She reached the nomination centre at about 3:07 p.m. and found the gates closed. Bhavani says an assistant to the Ward 12 candidate brought out a form and that she signed it between 3:20 and 3:30 p.m. after being put under pressure to withdraw.
When and by whom was the form submitted? When did the Returning Officer receive it, and on what basis was it accepted? We also seek clarity on why candidates in some other wards could remain in the race as independents and whether, as we understand, both alliance parties issued B forms in Ward 39.
Some Ward 11 residents asked us, “Why did she withdraw? We trusted you.” Hearing that was painful. Public trust in the alliance is built ward by ward. Young people take notice when someone raises a specific concern and gets a clear, documented answer.
I still trust you both. Please look into the records and show, through your response, the integrity and probity we expect from our government.

text:
深度用了 Neon 几天，我觉得这是一个 Sota 级别的模型，详细评价如下：

- 协作起来太舒服了，交流很顺畅，并且能懂你要做什么；
- 有时候会倾向于半途停下来，喜欢在工作到一半之后给你几个选项问你接下来要做什么，不过可以通过 AGENTS.md 修正；
- 速度还不错，能快速做出一个原型来验证，所以挺适合前端工作的；
- 有一定的设计和审美，很独特，但总体不如 Opus 5.5，不过我更倾向于说是互补而不是 Opus 5.5 全面更优；
- Coding 能力不如 Opus 5.5，或者说不如 Opus 那么“许愿式”，需要人工干预，One Shot 是绝对会出问题的；
- Review、Debug 能力还不错，所以你只要在让它干完活起独立审查，就能解决很多问题；
- 额度问题已经得到了非常大的优化，95%的缓存命中，Ultra 5x 能得到约 1.5B tokens 的 Neon 额度，20x 就是 约 6B，这个额度已经相当不错！

所以总体来说，这确实是个 Opus 5.5 的平替，很多方面不如 Opus 5.5，但可以在一定程度上弥补、修正；同时又有一些方面胜过 Opus，比如语言，非常的明显。综合下来非常推荐尝试订阅 Google AI Ultra！（建议月付，不要轻易上年订）

author: tulipking
quoted_text:
My simple mental model is that SoV tokens, especially alt SoV, are late cycle sinks for excess returns that are chasing further unbounded returns.

Basically, who wants to invest into $ZEC or pearl-2:native if you can invest at $HYPE, $LIT, $DRV etc at 10-20x (or historically cheap) revenue multiples?

Conversely, when nobody wants to buy those same names at 80x multiples, they pile into SoV tokens that are just momentum/sentiment trades unbounded by any ratio.

And then people go even further out on the risk curve into memes, and then even further out into stupid memes, and then everything crashes 80%.

Cheap revenue tokens create excess returns, excess returns create appetite for alt SoV, demand for alt SoV leads to misallocation of money/attention, misallocation of money/attention creates cheap revenue tokens.

今天他把原因讲清楚了。算力买下来，还要通电、散热、稳定跑起来，才收得到钱。中间哪怕只晚几个月，先付出去的钱还没变成收入，整个行业就要多垫几千亿美元的营运资金。钱从哪来？这是他自己问的。

现在的宏观，最怕就是没钱，没钱，没钱。 地主家也没余粮了
